title: Residue fields of closed points
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme of
finite type over a field
$K$, and let $x\in X$.

1. **(a)** $x$ is a closed point of
$X$ if and only if
$\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)=0$, i.e. if and only if
$\kappa(x)$ is finite over $K$ (Zariski's lemma: a field
finitely generated, as an algebra, over $K$ is finite over $K$).
1. **(b)** If $K$ is separably closed and $x$ is closed, then
$\kappa(x)/K$ is finite and purely inseparable and $\kappa(x)$ is
separably closed.

proof.text: Closed points have finite residue extension by the already proved source-library theorem Scheme.Hom.finite_residueField_of_isClosed (WeilConjectures.PointCount), which is the Jacobson/Zariski lemma argument. Conversely, Module.Finite makes Spec kappa(x) -> Spec K locally of finite type. Rewrite this morphism by Scheme.Hom.specMap_residueFieldAlgebraMap and apply locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp to Spec kappa(x) -> X. Since X is Jacobson by LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace, Mathlib isClosed_singleton_iff_locallyOfFiniteType makes x closed. This proves the second equivalence without choosing affine charts.

The residue extension is essentially of finite type. In the defining composite for f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x, the first map K -> kappa(f(x)) is essentially of finite type by the ideal residue-field instance in Mathlib RingTheory/LocalRing/ResidueField/Ideal.lean. The comparison isomorphism Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso has finite type inverse, since it is surjective. The last map is essentially of finite type by LocallyOfFiniteType.stalkMap and RingHom.EssFiniteType.residueFieldMap. Compose the three maps using RingHom.EssFiniteType.comp.

Mathlib trdeg_eq_zero_iff identifies transcendence degree zero with Algebra.IsAlgebraic. Finite residue extensions are algebraic by instance search; conversely the essentially finite type algebraic extension is finite by Algebra.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isAlgebraic. Combine with the equivalence of step 1. No transcendence basis is chosen.

Under IsSepClosed K and closedness of x, step 1 supplies Module.Finite K kappa(x), hence Algebra.IsAlgebraic K kappa(x). Apply the existing Mathlib leaves Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isPurelyInseparable_of_isSepClosed and Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isSepClosed, with F = K and E = kappa(x), and combine the three conclusions.
